comparability_caveat: NOT a clean A/B. Different corpus (regenerated with current code) AND a fresh set of LLM judge invocations; the panel is an LLM jury whose severity drifts run-to-run. The D22 measurement earlier this session showed exactly this: absolute panel percentages are a weak instrument, and a PAIRED blind A/B was the sharp one. Treat 13.0% as this corpus's honest floor under a forensic jury, NOT as proof of a 23-point regression.
what_holds: R1 market-scale routing 12/16 PASS (0 crit) and R4 business-model routing 12/16 PASS (0 crit) — the two dimensions earlier waves targeted are the ONLY two passing cleanly. Those fixes hold. Deterministic ring is 217/217 on the same corpus.
r8_diagnosis: R8 criticals 1 -> 11 (+10), the largest jump, in the dimension the discovery grounding touched. NOT mass mis-binding: only 2/282 resolved domains are <60d old, and spot checks resolve correctly (Airthings->airthings.com 5529d, Kaiterra->kaiterra.com 8214d). The mechanic is a SMALL mis-bind rate amplified: each error lands on a TOP-ranked competitor, then gets scraped, thesis-generated and priced into the benchmark (PurpleAir->purpleair.shop age 7d; One Skin->an Indian rupee storefront; Clay->Clay Labs GTM SaaS). Richer sets (density 23 vs 1-12) give the unfixed resolver more chances to land an error in the top 3. Judges also noted off_category was COMPUTED and then ignored ('the report itself identifies Jiffy as custom-apparel, but leaves off_category=false'). Root = the DEFERRED audit item 7 (relevance gate on tier-b/c domain resolution) + enforcing the off_category verdict — not a defect in the fan-out, whose brand NAMES a judge called 'a genuinely good category read' of the real industry.

harness_fix: This run is the FIRST valid one: two prior full runs died on a single random verifier ('Connection closed mid-response'), because the strict rule (any dead verifier -> INVALID) was paired with a one-shot attempt — at ~0.5% x ~117 verifiers, ~44% of runs were unverifiable. verifyWithRetry (3 attempts) fixed the EFFORT, not the rule. Measurement was stable across all three runs (pass=25 every time), so the number was never in doubt — only its validity.
